name: core.openwop.workflows.inbox
description: Real-work workflow pack (RFC 0013, ADR 0190 Phase 2) — the personal-productivity Inbox cluster: triage your own inbox (classify, draft the urgent reply, digest the rest), nudge unanswered threads, and debrief calls into coaching notes. Distinct from core.openwop.workflows.support (a customer-support mailbox with queue routing): these serve YOUR inbox and YOUR calls. Drafting uses core.email.draft — it creates a draft in your mailbox and never sends (the draft is the human gate); the one real send (follow-up nudger) waits on an approval. All tenant values are run parameters (replay-deterministic).
author: openwop

chains.label: Personal Inbox Triage
chains.description: Triage an email from YOUR inbox: classify it (urgent / needs-reply / FYI / newsletter), draft a reply INTO YOUR DRAFTS FOLDER when it needs one (never sends — you review and send), and deliver a one-line triage note. For a shared support mailbox with queue routing, use Support Email Triage instead.

emailText.description: The email body (with subject if available).

replyToAddress.description: The recipient address for a drafted reply (typically the original sender) — core.email.draft requires an explicit recipient; it cannot infer one from emailText.

replySubject.description: Subject line for a drafted reply.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: You are a personal inbox assistant. Classify this email: urgent / needs-reply / FYI / newsletter, with a one-line reason. If it needs a reply, list the points a reply must hit. End with 'REPLY: yes' or 'REPLY: no'. Email: {{params.emailText}}
Write a {{params.replyTone}} reply hitting every point the triage listed, in the first person.

chains.label: Follow-up Nudger
chains.description: Paste an email thread that went quiet and get a polite, context-aware follow-up drafted and sent — behind a human approval, because it leaves the building. Keeps the ask crisp and gives the recipient an easy out.

daysQuiet.description: How many days the thread has been quiet.

Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

senderEmail.description: Verified sender address these emails are sent from.

recipientEmail.description: The address this email is sent to.

emailSubject.description: Subject line for the sent email.

config.systemPrompt: Draft a short, polite follow-up to this thread, quiet for {{params.daysQuiet}} days: restate the one ask in a single sentence, offer an easy out ('if now isn't the time…'), keep it under 80 words, first person. Thread: {{params.threadText}}

config.title: Approve this follow-up before it is sent
